issue:
parse() ignores fill / align / width in field format specs

The format-spec grammar accepts fill, alignment and width — "{:>10}",
"{:<10}", "{:^7}", "{:*>6}" — but their semantics are ignored:

* "{:>10}" / "{:<10}" / "{:^7}" match, yet the captured value keeps the
  padding, so the round-trip parse(spec, spec.format(value)) does not
  recover `value`.
* A custom fill character ("{:*>6}", "{:-<6}") does not match at all.

Implement fill/align/width so parse() mirrors str.format() for these
specs:

1. A field with a width consumes exactly `width` characters.
2. Right-align ">" strips the fill character from the left of the
   captured value; left-align "<" strips it from the right; center "^"
   strips it from both sides. The default fill character is a single
   space.
3. Named fields ("{name:>8}") follow the same rule.

Acceptance criteria:

* The reproduction test
  tests/test_width_alignment.py::test_width_alignment_roundtrip
  (already committed, currently failing) must pass.
* The other new tests in tests/test_width_alignment.py (custom fill
  character, named field) must pass.
* The pre-existing suite (pytest tests/) must stay green (97 passed,
  1 skipped before this change).
* Do NOT modify anything under tests/ — the tests are the acceptance
  criteria. Implement the change in the parse package only.

Scope notes: values that legitimately contain the fill character are
inherently ambiguous and out of scope. Center alignment on the parse
side is defined as "strip the fill character from both sides".

Known landmines in the existing suite (all are acceptance criteria and
must pass UNMODIFIED — do not edit any file under tests/):

* tests/test_bugs.py::test_unused_left_alignment_bug and
  test_unused_centered_alignment_bug: when the value is LONGER than the
  specified width, the full value must still be captured (e.g.
  parse("{:<2S}", "foo")[0] == "foo"). Width is a lower bound, not a
  hard limit; str.format never truncates.
* tests/test_pattern.py::test_bi

profile.notes: Small Python package repository with 20 files; includes type stubs (.pyi), dependency automation, security policy, and CI configuration.

risks: The exact fill-stripping behavior is inherently ambiguous when the value legitimately contains the fill character, as explicitly out of scope.
Changing generated regular expressions may alter capture spans or numeric conversion behavior.
Treating width as an exact limit could truncate values longer than the width and break existing landmine tests.
Broadening alignment handling could accidentally change the legacy bare-alignment spec '{:>}'.
